picks.file: Merian d. Ä., Matthäus - Ansicht von Düsseldorf (1647).jpg
picks.what: View across the Rhine from the west, engraving in Merian’s Topographia Westphaliae
picks.why: whole riverfront skyline with St. Lambertus and the castle; outer border cut

picks.file: Jan van der Heyden and Adriaen van de Velde - View of Düsseldorf with the church of St. Andrew in the centre.jpg
picks.what: St. Andrew’s Church, painting (Mauritshuis, The Hague)
picks.who: Jan van der Heyden and Adriaen van de Velde
picks.why: color, the twin-towered St. Andreas recognizable; original rather than the later copy #3

picks.file: Stadtbild Düsseldorf von der Golzheimer Insel aus, um 1840, unbekannter Maler.jpg
picks.what: The Rhine bank and old town from the Golzheim island, painting
picks.why: color view with the leaning spire of St. Lambertus and the castle tower

picks.file: Düsseldorf from the Rhine, the Rhine, Germany-LCCN2002714104.jpg
picks.what: The old town from across the Rhine, photochrom print (Library of Congress)
picks.why: color riverfront with St. Lambertus; description dates it to the start of the Oberkassel bridge, about 1896; caption cut

picks.file: Rhein vor dem Ausbau 1962 bei Düsseldorf 1962-09-10 HBdia02187.jpg
picks.what: Aerial view of the old town, the Oberkassel bridge and the Rhine bend, color slide
picks.why: color aerial with St. Lambertus, the old town and the bridge; city shape clear

picks.what: The Rhine front at night with the castle tower, St. Lambertus and the Rhine Tower, photograph
picks.why: only modern skyline view; landmarks recognizable; empty night sky and water trimmed

gaps: P0: nothing; P6 is weak (night shot, temporary Ferris wheel)
notes: #3 is a later replica of #2. #4–#6 are 1828 lithographs after the 1667 painting, so not views of their own date. #7/#8 are river landscapes without the city. #23 Kiederich is dated only ‘before 1929’ (his death year), so #20 used for P5. #16 (Bleuler, before 1850) is a decent alternative for P3 but black and white and undated. Some writers treat the van der Heyden view (#2) as partly composed, but St. Andreas itself is accurate.
